context.body: Genesis through Deuteronomy distinguishes requests, responses, priestly formulas, intercession, restitution, pardon, retained consequence, and stated refusal to pardon. The bounded source is Exodus 34:4–10.

observations.body: The proclaimed divine name joins abundant covenant love and forgiving sin with refusal to clear guilt and generational visitation before Moses asks for pardon and inheritance.
observations.label: The proclaimed name forgives and does not clear: action

payload.posture: Read Exodus 34:4–10 as requests, law, and pardon evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The proclamation places forgiveness beside refusal to clear guilt and generational visitation; the relation must remain unresolved unless another source explicitly develops it.
